subject: Performance thresholds & hardware hedge plan for Novex Health
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novexhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Performance thresholds & next steps — post-demo recap

Thanks for the demo time this morning, Liam — quick recap and suggested next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Key constraints from the call:
- Latency target: 150 ms p95 for short-turn streaming responses (average 60–90 tokens).
- Throughput/steady-state: ~120 req/s across peak window (we heard 20 min burst patterns).
- Concurrency: up to ~50 simultaneous streams during peak.
- Streaming: client expects partial tokens every ~200–300ms; chunking behavior needs to be preserved.
- Data residency: US-only; audit logs required for pilot.

Redwood recommendation (high level):
1) Dedicated capacity pilot (reserved pool) to validate steady-state and burst behavior.
2) Hardware hedge: run parallel A100 and H100 microbenchmarks in our lab to measure streaming latency vs. cost. Early estimate: A100 offers slightly better cost/throughput for your prompt shape; H100 can reduce tail latency for very long sequences.
3) Pilot sizing: reserve throughput equivalent to 100 req/s for baseline with a 1.2x burst headroom (we'll measure real headroom during tests).

Deliverables we propose:
- Benchmark runbook with request profile (Ben will send the perf matrix).
- Pilot config (reserved throughput, concurrency caps, fallback policy).
- Cost estimate for 30-day pilot and scaling options.

Next steps / asks:
- Liam: share a representative request profile (sample payloads + typical token lengths) and a preferred 2-week window for the smoke test.
- Ben: run internal latency/throughput comparison and share the perf_matrix_v3.xlsx + a one-page attachment with the thresholds we discussed (attached).
- Priyom: please prepare an ops checklist for reserved pool provisioning and audit log access.

I attached a short thresholds draft (novex_perf_thresholds_v1.pdf). If this aligns, Ben and I can schedule the smoke test Wednesday or Thursday morning PST.

Thanks —
Rachel

Subject: Re: Performance thresholds & next steps — post-demo recap

Thanks Rachel — this is helpful. A couple clarifying points from our side before we lock dates: 

1) For streaming, we see most responses finish in ~80–120 tokens, but we have a small subset (~5%) that are 400–600 tokens. How aggressively will the pilot emulate that mixed profile? We want to ensure the tail behaviour is captured.
2) Can you include a rough delta in cost if we target 100 req/s vs 150 req/s for the pilot? We need a ballpark to get internal approval.
3) On hardware — if H100 reduces p99 by, say, 25% for long sequences, is it worth the extra cost for production? We might run a short A/B, but we need the tech recommendation.

We can provide a small anonymized sample request set (10k requests) and our traffic histogram by EOD Tuesday. Prefer smoke test Wed 09:00 PST if that works for your team.

—Liam

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novexhealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance thresholds & next steps — pilot plan and hardware matrix

Hi Liam — quick technical reply + attached perf matrix (spreadsheet includes tokens/sec, p95/p99 estimates, and cost curves). Summary up front:

Short answer on hardware: run a short parallel microbenchmark during the pilot. For your profile (80–120 tokens typical, 5% 400–600):
- A100 (40GB perf profile): best cost per token, solid throughput, predictable p95 for short sequences. Good if you optimize batching and KV cache hits.
- H100 (80GB stage): better p99/tail latency for long sequences and higher mixed-workload throughput, but higher hourly cost.
- Recommendation: baseline production on A100-equivalent configuration and gate H100 for the small tail-sensitive workloads; pilot should include 24–48hr H100 run to measure tail delta.

Sizing and reserved throughput (conservative starting point):
- Baseline reserved throughput: 100 req/s (covers steady-state and allows 1.2x burst).
- Concurrency cap: 60 streams (slightly above projected 50 to avoid headroom saturation).
- Token budget per request: default 1k tokens to accommodate long tails — billing/tracing will show actual usage.

Engineering notes (how we'll validate):
1) Continuous batching: we will configure a batching window tuned to maintain p95 < 150 ms for short responses while preserving streaming delivery (send-first-token latency target: <120 ms).
2) KV cache and prefix caching: for repeated context, we expect a 15–25% token compute reduction; please indicate reuse ratio in the sample dataset.
3) Fallback policy: configure a cheaper, quantized variant for non-critical traffic if queue depth exceeds burst headroom.

Attachments included: perf_matrix_v3.xlsx (detailed runs and cost curves). Also putting the threshold PDF Rachel attached into the shared folder and annotating rows with expected pass/fail gates.

Action items for the smoke test Wed 09:00 PST:
- Liam: upload anonymized sample payloads and histogram to the shared link (or send credentials).
- Priyom: provision the reserved pool (100 req/s, concurrency 60) and enable audit logs for the Novex tenant.
- Ben: run A100 baseline and 12–24 hour H100 tail run; share raw traces and aggregated p95/p99.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123
